I'm no Linux expert, but I've been using it since 2005 and let me tell you, it has save me from a lot of headaches. In that case is really hard to come up with an answer. Windows is closed source software, that means you can never be sure if an application is really doing what it says it does. Take the controversial updates for example: we can block the ones that clearly says ''windows telemetry tool'' or something like that, but nothing is stopping Microsoft from realeasing the same tracking code into an update named ''.NET security patch'' or some. We could all fall for it. The only way to investigate is doing what everyone has been doing: Tools like Wireshark can tell you what kind of data is being shared between those apps and MS servers.

But to be fair, that's not a Windows problem only. Like I said in the other thread, I try to use open source software on my smartphone as much as I can, as well. Android is Linux based, but the permissions system is fucking broken. You can install a flashlight app, and of course it works, but it also might be collecting sensitive data in the backgroud.

The only way to defend yourself from this is to be sure an app does and only does what it says it does, and an open code is half the task, the other half is learn to read code (or trust other people who can).
